correctness.rationale: For every integer r>=2 and every tuple n_i>=1 the adjacency 0-eigenspace projector is the direct sum of within-part contrasts. Its Schur square is positive on part-constant vectors and all internal contrasts except size-two pairs. The -1 projector is precisely the singleton contrast projector if there are two or more singleton parts, its Schur square removes every singleton direction except the difference when exactly two exist, and the Perron projector removes the unique singleton case. All spectral projectors have equal columns at the claimed twin pairs, so the remaining candidate difference vectors are in the common kernel. PSD of the Schur-square summands converts these to matching upper/lower nullity bounds. An independent 119-case numerical rank replay and 86-case exact rational projector replay corroborate, but do not prove, unrestricted quantification.

originality.rationale: The specific all-part-size adjacency Cesaro average mixing nullspace/rank classification is not among the verified theorems in inspected primary papers; Godsil and the 2017 commutant paper provide the spectral machinery, not the exact multipartite evaluation, while flexible randomized sampling and instantaneous uniformity address different quantifiers. Prior published results for complete graphs are covered special cases and are credited. The zero and minus-one projector argument and sharp singleton-pair exception supply additional conclusions. The literature comparison is limited: an implicit graph-scheme/twin-vertex formulation might subsume the claim.
residual_risks: A stronger formula under twin automorphisms, equitable partitions, coherent configurations or association schemes could imply this theorem without matching the queried wording.
A highly relevant 2026 Laplacian quantum-walk paper has not been inspected in full; its abstract speaks to different Hamiltonian and trace, not an exclusion of any unseen sections.
Searches of indexed records, while actual, cannot prove global uniqueness or rule out independent unpublished results.

value.rationale: The exact nullspace for every arbitrary complete multipartite graph resolves an entire natural infinite family of quantum average-mixing rank questions and sharpens the positive-definiteness criterion. Distinguishing independent twin pairs of size exactly two from adjacent singleton pairs exactly when their number is two is a structural boundary not predicted by an ordinary connectivity or adjacency rank argument. This is neither an arbitrary numeric slice nor merely a general formula substitution without a new closed invariant and kernel classification.
